anchor: SPT-Fence exhibits the \emph{same} race --- one shared logic flaw across two defenses ---  we find no independent SPT bug.
comment: The SPT-Fence race claim comes from pre-fix campaigns, and before the fix gem5-spt loaded zero branch annotations (no forced mispredict, no stall); the repo still marks A5 as open. After the fix, SPT_6_oneLP fence has 336|264 load hits and 28|22 new branch-transmitter hits, none triaged, so "no independent SPT bug" is unsupported.
proposed: Cut "we find no independent SPT bug"; say the SPT-Fence race is pending re-run on the fixed harness.

anchor:
squash drains; we observe \textbf{23{,}966} race instances and \textbf{0 at stock timing}, where the
defense holds.
comment: 23,966 is a pre-2026-10-30 number, and the figure plan says it isn't traced to any results path; 68/300 (UV6) is also pre-fix. Both are bolded as fact here and repeated as "validated" at the end of the section.
proposed: Mark both counts as pending re-run or replace them with [N] until a fixed-harness campaign exists.

anchor: $\sim$6.5$\times$ less total simulation to reach the bug (Fig.~\ref{fig:eff}).
comment: The arithmetic doesn't hold. At the stated per-test costs, SimSpect needs 6 x 0.092 = 0.55 s and AMuLeT needs 39 x 0.057 = 2.22 s, which is about 4x less simulation, not 6.5x. The 6.5x is the test-count ratio, and 0.092 vs 0.057 s (1.6x) is not "the same" per-test work.
proposed: Say ~4x less gem5 simulation time (6.5x fewer tests at ~1.6x the per-test cost).

anchor:
\textbf{\#6} versus AMuLeT's first contract violation at \textbf{\#39}: $6.5\times$ fewer tests, at
$\sim$7$\times$ the hit density (23\% vs.\ 3.3\%).
comment: This compares SimSpect's own pre-fix checker hits on a testset that is all the targeted single-load Spectre-v1 shape against AMuLeT's contract violations on random programs. The two use different leak bars and different stimuli, and all of SimSpect's SpecLFB numbers predate the harness fix.
proposed: State that the leak criteria differ and that the SpecLFB run is pre-fix (or re-run it); don't present 6.5x/7x as a like-for-like detection speedup.

comment: This is unfair as stated. The race manifests only at non-stock commitToIEWDelay (>=2-3; 0 leaks at stock), and the repo has no evidence that AMuLeT was ever run at that timing, so its missing the race says nothing about its search.
proposed: Say the race appears only at non-default squash latency, which AMuLeT's published setup doesn't sweep, or drop the claim.

anchor: and squash timing never disqualifies a load that already obtained its data.
comment: The repo contradicts this section's "every count is a confirmed real leak" bar. check_ld's data-obtained gate isn't bound to the window (it checks whether any instance at the transmitter PC ever sent a packet or completed), and on gem5-recon-modded reached_cache can't fire (unfixed). The section also omits the ReCon bugs: the OTB trace shows only an issue, not an access.
proposed: Weaken it to "in-window issue/execute, with a data-obtained gate" and list the gate limits, or cut the subsection until re-run.

comment: The bug explainer says the leak appears at commitToIEWDelay >= 3, or at 2 only when iewToCommitDelay is also raised. ">= 2" matches only the older PAPER_RESULTS summary, and the sweep predates the fix.
proposed: Say "leaks from 3 (2 when iewToCommitDelay is also raised)" and mark the sweep as pre-fix.

anchor:
while the resolved-branch stall is a flat plateau and the leak survives with the fnc stall off
(Fig.~\ref{fig:timing}b).
comment: These stall-knob conclusions come from pre-fix sweeps: the old resolve-stall hook froze runs when the CPU slept, and the old BTB force was wrong on every build. So "masks the leak, never manufactures one" and "flat plateau" are known-unreliable results stated as fact.
proposed: Drop the stall-knob sentence, or re-run it on the fixed harness first.

anchor: so its result is untainted while it still depends on a speculative load (Sec.~\ref{sec:bug-otb}).
comment: "SimSpect also exposes two bugs" overclaims for OTB. The Sec. bug-otb text itself says the Alloy enumeration doesn't reach this shape and the bug was shown with a hand-built test, and that trace shows only that i5 issues, not that it accesses the cache.
proposed: Say the OTB bug was found by hand-built test (SimSpect's interleave stage is meant to reach it) and that i5 issues early; cache access is pending an LSQ-traced re-run.

anchor:
\textbf{100\%} of \toolname{}'s tests carry a transmitter provably in the protection set, because
each test is enumerated \emph{to} place one there.
comment: The two percentages measure different things. AMuLeT's 17% counts window-valid speculative transmitter gadgets, while SimSpect's 100% is "in the protection set by our own model". After the fix, STT_6 on /work/stt gives 0 hits, so 100% targeting doesn't mean 100% of tests can leak.
proposed: Apply the same gadget-validity criterion to both tool's tests, or say the 100% is by construction under SimSpect's model.
